# How to Save Money with Cricut


-
-
-


15 September 2026


[Beth Baty](https://cricut.com/blog/author/bethb/)


---


Buying personalized gifts can add up quickly. A custom mug, monogrammed tote, personalized shirt, or wedding favor can cost considerably more than a similar item without customization.


That’s where Cricut can help. With your Cricut cutting machine or heat press, making personalized gifts and adding details yourself is a practical way to spend less while still giving something thoughtful and one-of-a-kind.


The key is knowing when handmade costs less than buying custom — and choosing projects, materials, and quantities that make your machine work in your favor.


Here’s how to save money with Cricut, from choosing the right projects to making the most of your materials.


## Why Cricut can be a cost-saving choice for personalized gifts


Personalization often comes with a premium. When you order a customized product, you’re paying not only for the blank item and materials, but also for design time, production, personalization, packaging, and the seller’s markup.


With Cricut, you can handle much of that yourself.


For example, instead of ordering a personalized tote for a teacher’s gift, you can buy a plain tote and add a name or design yourself using your Cricut cutting machine and heat press. The same approach works for mugs, shirts, drinkware, gift tags, home decor, party details, and much more.


Cricut is especially cost-effective when you:


- Have materials left over from previous projects
- Use affordable blanks
- Make several items at once
- Keep designs simple
- Personalize items you would otherwise purchase at a higher custom price


The biggest opportunity comes from projects where personalization would normally add a noticeable markup.


## Make vs. buy: when Cricut costs less than ordering custom


Before starting a project, compare the cost of making it with the price of buying a comparable personalized product.


Consider a personalized coffee tumbler. You can buy a tumbler in the color of your choice and add a name or design with vinyl. If you already have some vinyl on hand, even better, since your incremental material cost remains low.


Now compare that with ordering a personalized tumbler. The finished product includes the cost of the tumbler, personalization, production, and shipping.


These same calculations apply to:


- Birthday shirts
- Bridesmaid or wedding party gifts
- Holiday ornaments
- Gift tags
- Party favors
- Teacher gifts
- Name labels
- Simple home decor


The important thing is to compare like with like. A Cricut project isn’t automatically less expensive simply because you make it yourself. Your time, materials, and machine investment all have value.


A useful rule of thumb: the more personalization you need and the more items you make, the more opportunity there is for DIY savings.


## Cricut gift ideas that feel personal and cost less to make


Some of the best Cricut gift ideas combine an inexpensive blank with a small amount of personalization.


### Personalized mugs


A plain mug can become a thoughtful gift with a name, phrase, initials, or simple design. Mugs work well for birthdays, teacher appreciation, holidays, coworkers, and housewarming gifts.


You can also create several personalized mugs using a similar design, making the process more efficient when you have multiple gifts to prepare.


### Custom tote bags


Tote bags are versatile gifts for teachers, friends, bridal parties, book lovers, and family members. Add a name, monogram, favorite phrase, or simple graphic for a personalized touch.


Because the design can be relatively small, a single piece of vinyl can potentially stretch across multiple projects.


### Personalized T-shirts


Custom T-shirts are popular for birthdays, family gatherings, holidays, vacations, and celebrations. Making them yourself is particularly useful when you need several shirts with related designs; plus, you have a few different options for making T-shirts with your Cricut machine:


- Iron-On
- [DTF Transfers](https://cricut.com/blog?p=866980)
- Printable Iron-On
- [Sublimation and Infusible Ink™](https://cricut.com/blog?p=862978)


Instead of creating an entirely different design for every person, consider one design with interchangeable names or short phrases.


### Can coolers and drinkware


Personalized drinkware makes useful gifts for parties, weddings, birthdays, and holidays. Adding a name or monogram turns an everyday item into something made specifically for the recipient.


### Gift tags and packaging


You don’t have to make the entire gift to save money with Cricut. Small, personalized details make an affordable present feel much more special.


Try making:


- Personalized gift tags
- Card embellishments
- Stickers and labels
- Simple favor tags
- Envelope decorations
- Small gift-box accents


These smaller projects are also a great way to use leftover materials.


### Simple home decor


Names, initials, dates, and short phrases transform inexpensive blanks into personalized home decor. Think seasonal signs, labels, framed quotes, doormats, throw pillows, and small decorative pieces.


The trick is to choose projects where personalization adds meaningful value without requiring a huge amount of material or production time.


## Inexpensive gift ideas with Cricut for birthdays, teachers, weddings, and holidays


One of the easiest ways to get more value with your Cricut machine is to think about occasions where you need multiple gifts or coordinated items.


### Birthday gifts


For birthdays, consider personalized shirts, mugs, tote bags, drinkware, cake or party decorations, and gift tags.


If you’re already making decorations for a party, you may be able to use the same materials and design elements across several projects.


### Teacher gifts


Teacher gifts are a natural fit for making with Cricut because relatively simple items can easily become personalized keepsakes.


A customized tote, mug, notebook label, or classroom sign paired with another small item creates a thoughtful gift without requiring an elaborate project. Find these and several more ready-to-make teacher gifts from Design Space in our[teacher appreciation gift roundup](https://cricut.com/blog?p=863797) .


### Wedding gifts and details


Weddings often involve a long list of personalized details, from favor tags and signs to bridal party gifts.


This is an area where batching makes a particularly big difference. Instead of treating every item as a separate project, create one design and produce multiple copies.


For example, one design or cut can be adapted for a set of favor tags, place cards, or gift bags.[Check out our bridal guide](https://cricut.com/blog?p=868184) to getting the most out of your Cricut machine for your big day.


### Holiday gifts


Personalized ornaments, gift tags, mugs, shirts, stockings, and home decor are all great Cricut projects during the holidays.


Making several gifts with similar materials can also help you get more value from each package of vinyl, cardstock, or other supplies.[Check out our blog on gift-making](https://cricut.com/blog?p=740239) on a budget for tips and inspiration.


## Materials, blanks, and batching tips that lower project cost


The materials you choose can have a bigger impact on your project cost than the design itself.


### Choose blanks with the finished project in mind


Start by deciding what you’re making before buying supplies. An inexpensive blank that works well with your chosen material is more useful than buying a large quantity of something simply because it’s on sale.


For personalized gifts, look for blanks that are:


- Simple and versatile
- Easy to personalize
- Appropriate for the recipient
- Available in multipacks when you need several
- Compatible with the materials you plan to use


### Use fewer materials in each design


A design with several colors looks great, but it can also increase material use, preparation time, and the number of scraps left behind.


For many gifts, one-color designs are just as effective.


A simple statement design or a name, monogram, silhouette, or phrase creates a polished result without requiring multiple materials.


### Batch similar projects


Batching is one of the simplest Cricut hacks to save money.


If you’re making five personalized mugs, prepare all five designs together. If you’re making wedding favor tags, cut the entire batch at once.


Batching can help you:


- Reduce setup time
- Use materials more efficiently
- Minimize scraps
- Reuse the same design
- Catch mistakes earlier
- Make multiple gifts in less time


This is especially helpful when creating gifts for an event or holiday.


### Save and use scraps


Small pieces of vinyl, cardstock, and other materials can be useful for smaller projects.


Instead of throwing away every leftover piece, organize usable scraps by material, color, or size. Those pieces may be perfect for names, small labels, gift tags, or other compact designs.


### Reserve premium materials for high-impact details


Premium materials can make a project special, but you don’t necessarily need them for every part of it.


Use more economical materials for the main components and save specialty or premium materials for details where they’ll have the biggest visual impact.


## When Cricut saves money and when it does not


Cricut cutting machines can be a great tool for saving money, but DIY isn’t always the lowest-cost option.


If you need one item immediately, ordering may make more sense than spending hours designing and making it.


The same can be true when a project requires specialized equipment, techniques, or materials you don’t already have.


It’s also worth considering your time. If a personalized project takes several hours to make and the savings compared with buying it are minimal, the DIY option may not provide much value.


Before starting, ask yourself:


### What will the materials cost?


Include the blank, vinyl, cardstock, transfer materials, specialty supplies, and any other consumables.


### How many am I making?


One item may not offer much savings, while a batch of 10 or 20 similar items could make the DIY approach much more appealing.


### How long will it take?


Consider designing, cutting, weeding, assembling, and finishing the project.


### Do I already own the supplies?


Using materials you already have can change the economics of a project significantly.


### Could I simplify the design?


A simpler design can reduce both material costs and production time.


The goal isn’t to make everything yourself. It’s to identify the projects where Cricut gives you the best combination of personalization, affordability, and convenience.


## How to get more value from your Cricut machine


Once you start looking at projects through a cost-saving lens, small choices can add up. To keep costs low:


- Plan several projects around the same materials
- Use versatile blanks. Keep frequently used designs simple
- Save scraps for smaller projects
- Batch projects when you have several gifts to make


You can also build a small collection of reliable gift ideas that you can personalize for different occasions. A tote bag, mug, ornament, or gift tag can take on a completely different look with a new name, phrase, or design.


That flexibility is one of the biggest advantages of making handmade personalized gifts with your Cricut machine because you aren’t limited to whatever personalized options happen to be available for purchase.


## The bottom line: How to save money with Cricut


Learning how to save money with Cricut isn’t about making every gift yourself. It’s about recognizing when personalization is expensive to buy but relatively straightforward to create.


Start with projects where customization adds the most value: gifts, party details, teacher presents, wedding items, holiday decor, and everyday items that benefit from a personal touch.


Then make the savings work harder by choosing affordable blanks, batching projects, simplifying designs, and using your materials efficiently.


With the right project, a Cricut machine can help you create inexpensive personalized items that feel anything but inexpensive — that’s where DIY delivers the best value.

Yes, but it depends on the project. Cricut is most likely to save money when you already own the machine, choose affordable blanks, use materials efficiently, and make multiple personalized items. Always compare the total DIY cost — including your time — with the price of buying a comparable custom product.


####


Personalized gifts, party extras, labels, décor, teacher gifts, and wedding details can offer good opportunities for savings. These are categories where customization can add a significant premium to a ready-made product.


####


Some practical options include personalized mugs, tote bags, shirts, can coolers, ornaments, gift tags, and simple home décor. The best choice depends on what materials and blanks you already have and how much personalization you want to add.


####


Batch similar projects, choose lower-cost blanks, use fewer colors when possible, save usable scraps, and reserve premium materials for details that make a noticeable difference. Planning your projects before cutting can also help reduce wasted material.


####


Buying can make more sense when you need something quickly, are making only one complicated item, don’t already have the necessary materials, or would spend substantially more time making it than the potential savings are worth.
